metadata.title: Claude, Ic Memo.
metadata.purpose: NikBearBrown (Teardown) cut of claude-liam-ic-memo: take a Claude Skill apart, explain how the SKILL.md folder actually runs, and judge the design choices that make ic-memo repeatable and narrow at the same time.
metadata.carry_out: A Skill doesn't make Claude smarter — it makes Claude follow your steps, in order, every time.

beats.narration_text: Watch this. Someone types 'app' — because ic-memo looks like an app, feels like an app. It isn't. It's a skill. A folder of instructions Claude reads before it does anything. So the real question is: how does that folder draft the memo? Liam, in for Bear.

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types the naive framing, hesitates on 'app', corrects to 'skill'

props.text:
How does the
ic-memo app
write our memo?

beats.narration_text: Here's what's actually happening. A skill is a folder. Inside sits one file — SKILL.md, about two kilobytes — and that file is the entire instruction set Claude will follow. No hidden runtime, no compiled binary, no library reaching in from somewhere else. Plain English on the page. They optimized for legibility over cleverness: the whole program fits on a screen you can read, which is precisely why you can trust what it will do.

props.title: A skill is a folder.
props.calloutText: The SKILL.md is the instruction set.

beats.narration_text: The Steps section is the pipeline. Claude reads step one, does it, reads step two, does it — top to bottom, no branching unless a step tells it to branch. They chose linear execution over letting the model route itself. You give up the ability to be clever mid-run; you get back the ability to predict exactly what the run will do before it starts. That trade is the whole point.

ic-memo is a specification, not a suggestion. The instruction set says: draft a structured investment committee memo for PE deal approval, synthesizing due diligence findings, financial analysis, and deal terms into one document. Because Claude follows exactly what's written, the same inputs produce the same memo every run — and only that memo. It won't quietly reach past the page. This works if you value a repeatable, auditable draft; it fails the moment the deal needs a section the SKILL.md doesn't name.

props.heading: What the page says, exactly.
props.body: Draft an IC memo from diligence, financials, and deal terms.
props.sparkLine: Same page, same result, every run.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's a prompt you can paste directly into Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini — no CLI, nothing installed. Ask it to explain what a Claude Skill is, then to walk you through exactly how it would read and follow a three-step SKILL.md for drafting a one-page investment memo, step by step, before it starts drafting. Watching the model name the steps out loud before it acts is what proves the mechanism is real — Claude isn't inventing structure, it's following yours. Go deeper: what happens to the guarantee of same-input, same-output the moment a SKILL.md step tells Claude to 'use judgment' or 'pick the most relevant' — and how would you rewrite those steps so the skill stays predictable? Liam, in for Bear.
